latest_release.name: v0.0.17
latest_release.body:
**Subagents now work alongside you: switch between agents and run several fx instances in one window. Vercel Token Pass is now first-class in fx. Tool definitions 48.0% smaller, and 82.0% of later input from the prompt cache, up from 61.3%.**

### New Features

- Subagents work alongside the main agent and report back when they finish.
- Switch to any subagent to watch it, message it, or answer its prompts.
- A parent agent hears when its subagent's command has printed nothing for 2 minutes.
- Open the agent list with Down or Ctrl+X to see, search, switch, and close agents.
- Each subagent has its own model, effort, Fast mode, and permission mode, and subagents can nest two levels deep.
- The main agent sees its subagents each turn and reuses idle ones for related work.
- Agent profiles in `~/.fx/agents` or `.fx/agents` set an agent's tools, MCP servers, model, and prompt.
- `fx --profile <name>` starts a session in an agent profile.
- `fx --instances <n>` and `/launch` run several fx instances in one window.
- `fx sessions --live` lists open sessions and their subagents.
- `fx session <id>/<agent>` reads a subagent's conversation, and `--tail <n>` shows only the last turns.
- Vercel Token Pass models come first in the model picker.
- `/credits` and `fx credits` show your Token Pass credit and its reset date.
- Token Pass sessions use Token Pass models for titles, images, and auto mode review.
- Login offers Token Pass to teams that don't have it yet.
- The `toolbox` tool replaces `skill`, `capability_search`, and `mcp_select_tool`, so every request sends the same tools.
- `fx mcp call TOOL` runs an MCP tool from a shell command.
- Custom connections can set effort levels, request fields, headers, timeouts, and a title model.
- Cache warming keeps Claude's prompt cache warm while you pause, and `"cache_warming": false` turns it off.
- Reopening a session after a crash or a closed window sends the interrupted request again.
- Plain `fx` shows `Interrupted turn · /resume to continue` when a turn was left unfinished.
- `fx config` lists, reads, and changes settings.
- `fx ask --config key=value` overrides a setting for one request.
- `fx completion bash`, `zsh`, and `fish` print a shell completion script.
- `fx "<prompt>"` starts a session with that prompt, and `-r` is short for `--resume`.
- `FX_HOME` moves the profile folder from `~/.fx`.
- Ctrl+T cycles the reasoning effort.

### Improvements

- Toolbox raised prompt cache reads from 61.3% to 82.0% of later input in live tests across 9 model families.
- Built-in tool definitions are 48.0% smaller than in 0.0.16, and a new session's first request is 32.4% smaller.
- libfx's native addons are 10.1% to 12.9% smaller than in 0.0.16.
- The Linux arm64 and x86_64 binaries are 36.6% and 31.1% smaller than in 0.0.16.
- libfx requests now use AI Gateway's prompt cache.
- A shell result for a command with no output is about 70 characters instead of about 340.
- Skill descriptions in the toolbox menu stop at 200 characters, down from 1,024.
- Earlier turns go back to the model unchanged, so the prompt cache keeps covering them.
- An attached file's folder rules arrive as a note, so the prompt cache keeps matching.
- Conversations with many images drop the oldest in blocks, so the prompt cache stays valid longer.
- Amazon Nova models now use the prompt cache.
- Long sessions stay responsive, with the last turn of a 2,400-tool-call session taking 3 s instead of 11 s.
- Full detail in Ctrl+O shows each model call with its model, time, tokens, and call ID.
- `/trace` writes JSON Lines instead of a Markdown report.
- `/trace` includes subagents and keeps failed calls whole.
- Questions from the model render as Markdown.
- `fx doctor` now tests your credential and connects to each approved MCP server.
- Requests keep retrying through network drops, gateway errors, and rate limits until they succeed or you press Esc.
- Steering moves a running shell command to the background, so your message r

``` ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⣠⣾⣿⣿⣿⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀ ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⢰⣿⡿⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀ ⠀⠀⠀⣠⣶⣿⣿⣷⣶⡶⣶⣶⣆⠀⠀⠀⣴⣶⣶⠆ ⠀⠀⠀⠉⢹⣿⣿⠉⠉⠀⠘⢿⣿⣧⣀⣾⣿⡿⠃⠀ Tiny, open, embeddable, native coding agent. ⠀⠀⠀⠀⣼⣿⡏⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠻⣿⣿⣿⠟⠀⠀⠀ ⠀⠀⠀⢀⣿⣿⠃⠀⠀⠀⠀⢠⣦⠘⢿⣿⣷⡀⠀⠀ curl -fsSL https://fx.sh/setup.sh | bash ⠀⠀⠀⣸⣿⡟⠀⠀⠀⠀⣰⣿⣿⠗⠀⠻⣿⣿⣄⠀ ⠀⠀⠀⣿⣿⠇⠀⠀⠀⠾⠿⠿⠋⠀⠀⠀⠘⠿⠿⠦ ⚠ Status: Experimental. Use at your own risk. ⠀⣸⣿⡿⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀ ⣿⣿⣿⠟⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀ ``` # fx fx is a minimal coding agent CLI that still comes with batteries included. It's one native binary written in Zig, so there is no runtime to install, and it runs the same on your laptop, in CI, or inside an agent sandbox. Its output is closer to a Unix shell than an IDE, because the conversation prints into your terminal's scrollback instead of filling the screen. fx is meant to be embedded and extended. Scripts call it with `fx ask`, editors connect over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), and JavaScript apps run the same agent core through [libfx](sdk/README.md) with their own tools. Skills, MCP servers, and your project's `AGENTS.md` add to what the agent knows and can do.

## Features - **Small and fast**: CI fails a pull request if any benchmarked command, such as `fx help` or `fx status --json`, takes longer than 2 ms on Linux ([benchmarks](benchmarks/)). Stable releases for Apple silicon must also fit under a fixed size limit. - **Built-in tools**: fx finds, reads, and edits files, runs shell commands, searches the web and reads URLs, and delegates work to subagents. A development server or file watcher can keep running while it works ([tools](https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/tools)). - **Model choice**: sign in to Vercel AI Gateway, use a ChatGPT or Grok subscription, or connect an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint such as Ollama or OpenRouter ([custom model connections](https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/custom-model-connections)). - **Inline output**: you can scroll, search, and copy the conversation like any other command's output, and tmux bindings and copy mode keep working. Terminals that support the [Program Status Protocol](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status) can also show when fx is busy or waiting for you. - **Your own shell**: commands run in your login shell, with your aliases, functions, and `PATH`. fx runs your startup files once and reuses the result until one of them changes, so a slow `.zshrc` doesn't slow down every command. Commands also receive `AI_AGENT=fx` in their environment, so development tools can detect fx. - **Permissions**: the default `auto` mode runs routine work, such as editing project files and running tests, without asking. Anything else goes first to a model that checks the exact action for prompt injection or malicious behavior, and fx holds the action if the check finds a problem. Switch to `ask` to approve each action yourself, or to `full-access` to turn the checks off ([permissions](https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/permissions)). - **Sessions**: fx saves your conversations under `~/.fx/sessions/`, and `fx -c` picks up where you left off in a project. When a conversation fills the model's context, fx compacts older turns but keeps their full text on disk, where the agent can look it up ([sessions](https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/sessions)). ## Install ```bash curl -fsSL https://fx.sh/setup.sh | bash ``` fx runs on macOS and Linux, on x86_64 and arm64. The installer puts it in `~/.local/bin`. fx checks for updates in the background, and `fx upgrade` installs the latest release right away. [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) lists what changed in each release. You can also [try fx in your browser](https://fx.sh/try) without installing anything. ## Quick start Sign in with one of these: ```bash fx login # Vercel AI Gateway fx login codex # ChatGPT subscription fx login grok # Grok subscription fx login vercel --api-key # AI Gateway API key ``` Then open a project and start fx: ```bash cd your-project fx ``` Type what you want done and press Enter. `/help` lists the slash commands. If something doesn't work, run `fx doctor` to check your setup. To send one request without the interactive shell, use `fx ask`. Add `--json` when a script needs to read the result: ```bash fx ask "explain the changes in this repository" fx ask --json "summarize the failing tests" | jq -r .final_output ``` ## Embed and extend | Surface | Use it for | | --- | --- | | fx ask | One request from a script or CI job. `--json` returns structured output, and `--resume` continues a saved session. | | fx acp | Editors and other [Agent Client Protocol](https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/acp) clients, over stdio. | | [libfx](https://www.npmjs.com/package/libfx) | The agent core as a JavaScript library, built as a native Node.js addon and as WebAssembly. `createFxAgent()` runs an agent with your own tools, MCP clients, and skills, and `createFxTerminal()` embeds the fx terminal. | The [libfx README](sdk/README.md) and the [libfx docs](https://fx.sh/docs/lib) cover the API. The WebAssembly build is experimental. The CLI also picks up these extensions: - **Skills**: fx loads skills from `.fx/skills` and `~/.fx/skills`, and from the folders other agents use, such as `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`. The model sees each skill's name and description and reads the full instructions only when it needs them, so installed skills take little room in the context ([skills](https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/skills)). - **MCP servers**: `/mcp add slack` sets up Slack, and `fx mcp` manages servers from your terminal. A server's tool schemas load when the model looks for them ([MCP](https://fx.sh/docs/capabilities/mcp)). - **Project instructions**: fx follows the `AGENTS.md` in your project, nested `AGENTS.md` files for the directories they cover, and `~/.fx/AGENTS.md` for your own instructions across projects ([project instructions](https://fx.sh/docs/configure-fx/project-instructions)). ## Examples [`examples/`](examples) has small libfx apps you can run with an AI Gateway API key: - [`node-chat`](examples/node-chat): a terminal chat with streamed replies. - [`browser-agent`](examples/browser-agent): the agent in WebAssembly behind a plain HTML form. - [`nextjs-agent`](examples/nextjs-agent): a Next.js App Router form with a streaming route handler. - [`nuxt-agent`](examples/nuxt-agent): the same idea in Nuxt, with a Nitro route. ## Documentation The manual at [fx.sh/docs](https://fx.sh/docs) covers models, permissions, configuration, skills, MCP, sessions, and every CLI and slash command. ## For coding agents To learn fx, read the manual as Markdown. [fx.sh/llms.txt](https://fx.sh/llms.txt) indexes every page, [fx.sh/llms-full.txt](https://fx.sh/llms-full.txt) puts the whole manual in one file, and adding `.md` to any docs URL returns that page as Markdown. For the flags of the installed version, run `fx --help`. To run fx from your own tools, use `fx ask`. It takes the prompt as arguments or on stdin, writes its result to stdout and progress and diagnostics to stderr, and exits with a nonzero status when the request fails. With `--json`, the final answer is in `final_output`. To inspect a user's setup, run `fx status --json` for configuration and runtime information, or `fx doctor --json` for health checks. Neither changes the setup. `fx ask` uses the user's saved permission mode, which is `auto` unless they changed it. Pass `--full-access` only when the user asks for it, because it turns off fx's permission checks. To change fx itself, read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) first, then build and verify the change as described in [Contributing](#contributing). ## Feedback Run `/feedback` inside fx to open the feedback form, or [open an issue](https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx/issues/new/choose). If something looks wrong in your terminal, `/trace` creates a private diagnostic trace that you can share as a link from [fx.sh/share](https://fx.sh/share) ([share feedback](https://fx.sh/docs/using-fx/share-feedback)). ## Contributing You need [Zig 0.17.1](https://ziglang.org/download/) to build fx: ```bash git clone https://github.com/vercel-labs/fx.git cd fx zig build ./zig-out/bin/fx ``` Test your changes with the freshly built `./zig-out/bin/fx`, because a bare `fx` may be an older copy on your `PATH`. `zig build test` runs the unit tests, which sit next to the code they cover. The end-to-end tests in [`tests/e2e/`](tests/e2e) drive the built binary through tmux and need [Bun](https://bun.sh). The source is laid out like this: ```text fx/ ├── src/ │ ├── main.zig entry point that wires everything together │ ├── core/ agent loop, sessions, config, permissions, MCP, skills │ ├── builtins/ built-in tool specs, providers, and the system prompt │ ├── tools/ built-in tools: files, shell, web, skills, subagents │ ├── ui/ terminal rendering and input │ ├── gateway/ model provider transport │ ├── mcp/ MCP engine │ └── acp/ Agent Client Protocol server ├── sdk/ libfx, the JavaScript library ├── tests/ end-to-end tests and model evals └── benchmarks/ startup, memory, and latency benchmarks ``` Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before you open a pull request. It covers verification, CI, and PR labels. If a coding agent is helping you, point it at [For coding agents](#for-coding-agents). ## Security Report vulnerabilities through the [contact page](https://fx.sh/contact) instead of a public issue. ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE). Third-party licenses and attributions are in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## Credits Interface sounds by [cuelume](https://github.com/Danilaa1/cuelume).
